questions.question_text: Differentiate clearly between Mass and Weight across 3 distinct parameters.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Definition: Mass is matter quantity; Weight is gravitational pull force. 2. SI Unit: Mass in kg; Weight in N. 3. Constancy: Mass is constant everywhere; Weight changes with gravitational acceleration g.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study Questions)

questions.question_text: Classify forces into contact and non-contact types, giving two detailed examples for each.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Contact Forces (require physical contact): a) Muscular Force: Exerted by anatomical muscle contraction (e.g. pulling a cart). b) Frictional Force: Surface roughness opposing relative motion (e.g. shoe soles gripping ground). 2. Non-Contact Forces (act across distance): a) Gravitational Force: Mutual attraction between masses (e.g. Earth pulling falling rain). b) Electrostatic Force: Force between electric charges (e.g. charged balloon sticking to neutral wall).

questions.marking_scheme_answer: Contact forces require physical touching (muscular, friction). Non-contact forces act across distance through fields (gravity, electrostatic attraction/repulsion, magnetic pole forces).
